text:
An approval screen is only part of the evidence.

CERT-In reports an AI-assisted campaign targeting Indian financial entities through their payment interfaces. Its earlier advisory describes stolen credentials enabling direct payment calls that bypass application checks.

To me, that makes the leadership issue concrete: seeing an approval does not establish that the system moving the money requires it.

A screen can show the intended decision. The harder question is whether the final transfer must match that decision, including the recipient and amount. If those can diverge, a reassuring display offers little assurance about the payment itself.

My recommendation is to have the business and IT owners trace one approved payment together, from the decision through to transfer. Ask them to demonstrate what prevents a payment proceeding when its details differ from the approval, or when approval is absent.

That gives leaders something more useful than a walkthrough of screens: evidence that the permission granted actually governs the money moved.
